findings.problem: MetricWorkflow uses status: String plus is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool, allowing illegal combinations at compile time (e.g. status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with status="draft"). SKILL.md line 35 explicitly requires enum/typestate state machine for this pattern.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a MetricWorkflow with contradictory fields, producing a domain state the rest of the system cannot reason about correctly. No invariant is enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed MetricStatus enum (Draft, Validated, Sent). Replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a MetricState enum (Init, Validated, Sent) that encodes the lifecycle as a typestate. Remove sent_at_epoch_ms and add it only on the Sent variant, or use a newtype timestamp value object.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics. Functional-core-performance reference line 16: 'Replace bool lifecycle flags, status strings, and Option lifecycle fields with enums or typestates' — the same principle applies to IDs: they should be newtyped.
findings.failure_mode: Any String can be used as a metric ID, including empty strings, malformed IDs, or IDs from the wrong namespace. The core cannot assume validity by construction.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype struct MetricId(String) with a fallible constructor that validates the ID format, and use MetricId instead of String in MetricWorkflow.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes MetricWorkflow by value and mutates fields directly (item.status = "sent".to_string(), item.is_sent = true) instead of using an enum-based state transition. This is a mutation-based lifecycle, not a state machine.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called on a MetricWorkflow in any state, including ones that should not be markable-as-sent (e.g. not yet validated). There is no compile-time guarantee that the workflow is in the correct pre-state for the transition.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with an enum-driven state machine. Use a fallible transition method like fn validate(self) -> Result<MetricWorkflow<Validated>, MetricError> and fn send(self) -> Result<MetricWorkflow<Sent>, MetricError> that enforce pre-state requirements at compile time. The struct should be generic over a state type parameter (typestate pattern).

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String on every call and discards the previous status string without any error handling or state transition validation. This is hidden side-effect allocation with no typed error path.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation failure is silently ignored (the panic would only occur on OOM). More importantly, the previous status is lost without any audit trail or error, violating the railway error taxonomy.
findings.fix: Remove the mutable status field entirely. Use an enum variant to carry the state. Eliminate String allocation in state transitions.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any stated performance claim
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no capacity planning anywhere in the crate)
no second-ring evidence (no formal verification, no property tests, no Kani/Verus/Flux artifacts)
no command evidence (no cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy output)
no error taxonomy defined — ParseError, FrameError, Allocation, or domain error types are absent
residual_risk: The struct admits every illegal state combination at compile time with no enforcement. mark_sent is a blind mutation with no pre-condition check. Static review only; no commands run. Without enum/typestate state machine, any downstream code reading status and is_sent independently will see contradictory values and cannot safely branch on them.
